Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

rxode2lincmt (development version)

New features

  • The linCmt() sensitivity carry is read from rxode2’s solve buffer (ind->solve) when rxode2 sends its carry states (the new host-table rows numLinCarry, linCmtCarryRow and n_all_times), sized to each model, so it has no cap; .linCmtCarryMaxPairs() reports .Machine$integer.max then. With an rxode2 that does not send them the carry stays in the fixed 8-pair array, as before.

Bug fixes

  • At a confluence the one to three compartment solutions divided by a vanishing difference of rates: an absorption rate at a disposition rate, two nearly equal disposition rates, a near-zero elimination under an infusion, a disposition rate far below the largest – in the time-propagation solutions and the steady states alike. That gave a NaN amount (two and three compartment oral models, oral steady states), a wrong ka gradient at an exact one compartment confluence, and values and derivatives that lost their digits near one. Inside those bands (one rule over the rates the solution is built from) the step and the steady states are now computed from the matrix exponential of the compartment generator, which has no rate differences and no eigenvalues; outside them the closed forms run unchanged (bitwise). Every case of a 60-digit reference now matches to 1e-10 in value and 1e-9 in gradient (#18).
  • Internal test hook .linCmtHostSim() solves a synthetic subject through linCmtA()/linCmtB() on stand-in solver structs, so the solver paths are tested without rxode2.

Bug fixes

  • The per-compartment dose-time and bioavailability sensitivities (linCmtB() which1 = -9 and -10) are no longer NA at a record the solve does not advance: one at the same time as the record before it, such as an observation at a dose time. Such a record had no decomposition of its own; it now takes the last advanced record’s, plus the doses given at that time. nlmixr2est’s FOCEi reads the -10 sensitivity at every observation, so a linCmt() model with an eta on f() failed every subject that had a sample at a dose time, and its fit returned a constant objective. At an infusion start the dose-time read uses the started rate; a model tracking no origin still reads NA.

  • linCmtModelDouble() no longer crashes R with the finite-difference sensType values 1, 2, 10 and 20: it now computes the base value first, as linCmtB() does, and all four use the step sensH.

  • The four-point forward difference that linCmt() finite-difference gradients fall back to with linCmtForwardMax = 3 used the coefficient 6 instead of 2 on its last point, so a suspect gradient came out wrong. The default (linCmtForwardMax = 2) is unchanged.

rxode2lincmt 0.1.1

New features

  • linCmtB() now gives second-order sensitivities: which1 = -20 reads the Hessian of an amount and which1 = -21 that of the central concentration, over the full parameter order. They are kept, with a quadratic carry of the dose history, only for a model that asks for them (ndiff bit 128), so other models are unchanged. A modeled bioavailability is followed (it scales a parameter-free dose amount). Rows whose carry these parameter-space Hessians do not follow – finite-difference sensitivities, a modeled lag, rate or duration, replace and multiply records, parameters that change between records, and any row advanced on a path that keeps no Hessians – read NA, never a silent zero (#17).

  • linCmtModelHess() advances one step with the value, Jacobian and Hessians, the second-order counterpart of linCmtModelDouble() (#17).

  • An eta-space second-order carry, driven by linCmtB() sentinels (which1 = -30 to -38), gives the exact first and second derivatives of the amounts and the concentration in the random effects when the parameters change between records (a time-varying covariate) and through a modeled bioavailability on boluses. Each row passes its own dp/deta and d2p/deta2 (and dF/deta, d2F/deta2); the step is differentiated through them, and the interval takes the parameters the solve itself used, so locf and nocb interpolation are both followed. The generated model has to emit the sentinels; this is the runtime the estimator’s code generation builds on (#19).

  • The second-order steps can be switched per thread: the C callable linCmtSetHessThread() (registered for R_GetCCallable(), detected by the internal .linCmtHessThread()) says, on the solving thread, whether the model being solved reads them. rx->ndiff is one field shared by every model an estimator solves concurrently, so an estimator that keeps the second-order bit on for all of them uses this to spare the models that never read a Hessian. The second-order history also starts over when a subject is solved again, and a record at the initial state reads zero rather than NA.

  • linCmt() FOCEi fits spend less time per row: the output pass that runs after each solved interval now takes the thin value path instead of restoring the full Jacobian, the AD path copies the requested parameters instead of running the scaling setup, and the value-memo check runs before the rest of the per-row work. Results are bitwise unchanged (#2).

  • linCmt() value-only solves (SAEM, rxSolve() simulation, pred-only solves) return an already-solved row before any model setup. Results are bitwise unchanged (#9).

  • linCmt() value-only solves no longer allocate on each computed row. Results are bitwise unchanged (#9).

  • linCmt() value-only solves compute the micro-constants and the 2- and 3-compartment eigen-decomposition once per parameter set instead of on every row. Results are bitwise unchanged (#9).

Bug fixes

  • The linCmt() sensitivity carry, which ‘nlmixr2est’ uses for the FOCEi gradient of a linCmt() parameter with a time-varying covariate, now restarts at a reset (EVID 3, and the reset an EVID 4 begins with). The reset zeroes the compartments, but the carried sensitivities and their trackers kept their values from before it, so such a fit with a reset was off the same model written as ODEs (0.063 in the objective with an EVID 4 under nocb). A replace (EVID 5) or multiply (EVID 6) record, from the data or pushed by evid_(), now zeroes or scales the replaced compartment’s carried sensitivities, which used to keep their values. The carried gradient after such a record is exact only together with linCmtEventJac(), which makes this package’s own Jacobian follow the event; without it, it is no worse than before. With f() or alag() modeled on the compartment the carry does not know a multiply’s factor and leaves that compartment’s sensitivities as before.

  • The last-row value memo of linCmt() never hit inside an ‘nlmixr2est’ fit, because ‘nlmixr2est’ leaves the finite-difference step NaN and NaN never equals itself; every repeated call the model makes for a row recomputed it. The memo keys now compare bitwise (#2).

rxode2lincmt 0.1.0

CRAN release: 2026-09-24

New features

  • Initial release. The analytic one, two and three compartment linear solutions, their ‘stan’ gradients, the eigen decompositions (solComp2(), solComp3()) and the derived-parameter conversions behind rxode2::rxDerived() moved here from ‘rxode2’, so ‘rxode2’ no longer compiles ‘stan’. ‘rxode2’ reaches the compiled kernels through an external-pointer table and hands this package the struct offsets it needs, so neither package shares struct layouts with the other.

  • The package neither links nor loads the TBB library: the ‘stan’ autodiff tapes are created per thread here, so ‘RcppParallel’ is needed only for its headers.

  • The closed-form solutions follow the idea of the ‘wnl’ package by Kyun-Seop Bae; the implementation here is different.
